title: Raspberry Frozen Yoghurt
changes_from_base: A short 1-2 h strain, sieved macerated raspberries and warm sweetened milk replace the long strain; golden syrup still keeps it smooth.
summary: A bright pink raspberry frozen yoghurt, sieved seed-free and kept smooth with a little golden syrup.

ingredients.note: 50 g for the berries, 100 g for the milk

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Spoon the 500 g yoghurt into a fine sieve over a measuring jug and chill for 1-2 h until about 120 ml liquid has drained. Discard the liquid.

steps.title: Macerate
steps.text: Mash 500 g fresh raspberries lightly with 50 g caster sugar and 1 tsp vanilla, leave 1 h at room temperature, then sieve out seeds.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm the 240 ml milk with 100 g caster sugar in a small saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Take it off the heat, stir in the 3 tbsp golden syrup and leave to cool.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Mix the milk mixture and raspberry purée into the drained yoghurt in a bowl.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill the mixture until 4 °C or colder using an instant-read thermometer.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn the cold mixture in the ice-cream maker until frozen and thick.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve it soft straight away, or spoon it into a lidded container and firm up in the freezer for 1-2 h.

tips: Thawed frozen raspberries are just as good as fresh here.
Golden syrup keeps the texture soft without any setting agent.
Scatter a few whole raspberries over each bowl to serve.
storage: Best within 1 day; keep in a lidded container in the freezer and soften 10 min before scooping, as it turns icy after that.
